sources.title: Agent Client Protocol v1 Initialization

evidence.passage: Clients and Agents MUST treat all capabilities omitted in the `initialize` request as UNSUPPORTED.

supported_claims: ACP initializes before session creation, negotiates version and supported capabilities, and treats absence as unsupported.
v1 baseline session operations are new, prompt, cancel, update; richer session methods are optional.
inferences: Use an explicit minimal adapter contract and optional typed capability providers; do not silently assume hook delivery or child attribution for an unknown harness.
Bind observed version and admitted capability set into a runtime session object instead of scattering repeated probes through callers.

sources.title: Agent Client Protocol v2 Migration

evidence.locator: Session setup and lifecycle / Baseline methods

supported_claims: v2 changes capability shape and makes list/resume/close baseline when session is advertised; v1 loadSession and session/load disappear.
inferences: Capabilities must have a named semantic contract/version, not a timeless boolean bag.
The herdr adapter interface should not import ACP's entire evolving protocol surface merely to gain extensibility.

sources.title: ACP adapter for Codex CLI README

evidence.passage: It starts the Codex App Server
enabled only after bilateral capability negotiation

supported_claims: codex-acp hosts an ACP stdio server and translates Codex App Server requests/events, rather than decorating an already-running TUI with hooks.
Its npm package includes a compatible Codex dependency and offers CODEX_PATH override.
Native subagent sessions are negotiated; unsupported peers receive ordinary ACP tool-call representation.
inferences: A compatible dependency pin is a concrete example of recipe/version ownership; a bare executable name cannot certify integration behavior.
Do not mistake a mapped child display or fallback root interaction for authenticated child identity/provenance.
Adopting ACP would replace the interaction model and broaden process/auth/permission ownership; this is larger than introducing local harness adapters.

sources.title: ACP adapter for the Claude Agent SDK README

evidence.passage: child interactions stay on the root session

supported_claims: Current claude-agent-acp uses the Claude Agent SDK.
Its README describes SDK control API handling for MCP actions refused in SDK mode.
Native child sessions require bilateral negotiation; absent that signal, child lifecycle is ordinary tool-call representation on the root session.
inferences: An adapter needs integration-mode-specific capability evidence; CLI hooks, SDK control, and ACP hosting are different backends even when the harness brand is identical.
Preserve native permission refusal rather than claiming wrappers manufacture unavailable approval functionality.

sources.title: hcom README

evidence.passage: Hooks activate only when an agent is launched with `hcom` in front.
Any other AI tool without hooks can join

supported_claims: hcom coordinates multiple existing CLI agents through hooks and a shared database.
Its integration is activated by launch rather than ordinary CLI usage.
Its README offers a manual fallback for agents without hooks and hook removal tooling.
inferences: This is the closest scoped prior art for herdr: normalize existing harness hooks while retaining user-owned terminal/runtime.
Separate launcher-only/manual support from automatic native integration; allow a future adapter to expose partial capabilities honestly.
Setup/unsetup should identify owned modifications and preserve foreign config; README claims safe removal, but removal implementation was not audited.

sources.title: hcom shared hook infrastructure Rust source

evidence.passage: Each tool's raw hook JSON is different.
Delivery ack to commit after stdout is successfully written.

supported_claims: HookPayload normalizes multiple harness inputs into common fields, including optional session/transcript identifiers and retained raw payload.
Its common module contains separate harness-specific constructor functions.
HookResult models Allow, Block, and UpdateInput; delivery acknowledgments are documented to commit after stdout write.
inferences: Shared normalized observations are useful, but central from_claude/from_codex constructors still require central edits for each harness; place decode/output mapping inside each registered adapter.
Keep optional absence explicit; transcript_path=None is preferable to invented evidence.
A normalized effect must retain output delivery/ack ordering; output rendering is part of the adapter contract, not a generic successful receipt assumption.
Copying a global normalized result with universal exit code meanings can erase event-specific differences; adapter output encoding should validate which native event admits each effect.

contradictions.issue: Older Zed Codex adapter location versus maintained implementation
contradictions.resolution: https://github.com/zed-industries/codex-acp is archived and points to agentclientprotocol/codex-acp; use the maintained App Server implementation for current architecture facts.

contradictions.issue: Search results call Claude adapter a CLI wrapper, current maintainer README calls it Agent SDK adapter
contradictions.resolution: Use current README; do not assume native TUI hook semantics from ACP support.

contradictions.issue: ACP site default initialization redirects to v1 while repository also contains v2 documentation
contradictions.resolution: Record protocol version explicitly. This bounded audit does not establish every client's released v2 support.

contradictions.issue: hcom indexed README variants disagree on global first-run activation versus launch-only activation
contradictions.resolution: Current raw main README describes launch-only activation. Treat runtime behavior as unverified until code/version is pinned.

gaps: No native installation or runtime tests were performed; documentation/code evidence is not native PASS.
Main-branch sources are mutable, not commit-pinned; pin selected code snapshots before turning them into release claims.
hcom setup/removal implementation, receipt persistence, and provenance policy were not audited within the four-batch budget.
Attempted hcom src/core/tools.rs fetch returned Internal Error and supports no claims.
An unknown future harness may lack native context injection or stable session IDs; interface implementation can represent this limit but cannot create those capabilities.
recommendation_inference: Use a small built-in registry of Rust HarnessAdapter implementations returning typed optional capability objects and an admitted runtime session/recipe. Each adapter owns launch/config footprint, native event decode and output encoding. Keep canonical attribution/receipt transitions in the daemon and require evidence provenance on normalized observations. Avoid a new universal network protocol or ACP dependency in this refactor. Test a deliberately limited fake adapter to ensure missing features fail explicitly without new core match arms.
retrieval_stop: Four query/fetch batches complete; primary-source evidence sufficient for design tradeoffs. Runtime, ownership implementation and version pinning are explicit follow-up gaps.
